title: Hash map
summary: Any key finds its value in one jump, like a letter dropped straight into the right pigeonhole.

viz.hello: This hash map has {n} buckets and holds {count} keys. Type a word as the key and a number as the value, then press put. Try get on idli to watch a chain being searched.
viz.badKey: A key here is 1 to 8 letters, a to z. Try a word like chai or puri.
viz.hashed: {key}: adding up its letter codes gives {hash}. {hash} % {n} = {index}, so it belongs in bucket {index}.
viz.putEmpty: put({key}, {value}): bucket {index} was empty, so {key} goes straight in.
viz.putCollision: put({key}, {value}): bucket {index} already holds {others}. That is a collision. {key} is chained in at the front and the others move along.
viz.putUpdate: put({key}, {value}): {key} is already in bucket {index}, so only its value changes: {old} -> {value}.
viz.compare: Is this {key}? No, it is {other}. On to the next entry in the chain.
viz.found: Found {key} in bucket {index}: its value is {value}. Keys compared on the way: {steps}.
viz.notFound: get({key}): bucket {index} does not have {key}. Keys compared: {steps}. Nowhere else needs searching.
viz.notFoundEmpty: get({key}): bucket {index} is empty, so {key} is not in the map. One look, no searching.
viz.removed: remove({key}): unlinked {key} from the chain in bucket {index}. The entries behind it close the gap.
viz.removeMissing: remove({key}): {key} is not in bucket {index}, so there is nothing to remove.
viz.growing: {count} keys already fill {n} buckets. One more would crowd the chains, so the table grows to {m} buckets and every key is hashed again.
viz.growCap: The playground stops at {n} buckets so the picture fits. A real hash map would keep doubling, and its chains would stay short.
viz.loadNote: A hash map keeps about one key per bucket on average, so chains stay short and get stays fast.
viz.resetDone: Started again with an empty table of {n} buckets.
